_README: Every place in src/ that opens the CANONICAL VAULT with its own `new Database(...)`,
bypassing the adapter chokepoint (src/adapter/d1.js) and therefore bypassing the
fail-stop latch, the corruption marker and the standard pragmas.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the vault's durability guards were added one per incident, and
each new opener could silently miss all of them. Counting them was never possible, so
nobody knew the guards had holes. `maxWriteCapable` is a RATCHET: it may only shrink.
A new unguarded opener cannot land; an existing one can only be removed or downgraded.
This is a build-time invariant, not another runtime guard. It does not detect damage —
it prevents the class of mistake where a guard is added and then quietly routed around.
readOnly openers are SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: they cannot write to a damaged vault, which
is the property the latch exists to enforce. Moving an opener from writeCapable to
readOnly is the cheapest way to shrink the ratchet, and is usually possible — VACUUM
INTO, for one, succeeds on a read-only connection (measured 2026-07-28).

NOT_THE_VAULT (scripts/verify-vault-open-chokepoint.mjs) exempts openers that are not the vault at all. src/db/vault-lease.js is one: it opens `.vault-ownership`, a zero-row file whose ONLY purpose is to carry a kernel (fcntl) lock. It holds no data, so it is neither a vault opener nor a write of any kind that the fail-stop latch could care about.

readOnly.why: key probe — opens readonly to test whether a key opens the vault; cannot write
verifyVaultIntegritySync — the read-only quick_check that decides whether a flagged vault is still damaged
VACUUM INTO from a readonly handle; also refuses outright on .vault-corrupt
export archive VACUUM INTO / .backup() from a READ-ONLY handle

D-130 off-loop copy child: VACUUM INTO from a READONLY src handle (both its opens — src, and the readonly verify handle on the produced .tmp). Read-only is safe HERE, unlike the sync twin in snapshot-on-boot.js, because this child has exactly one launch context: awaited from initVaultStorage while the parent holds the cross-process init lock, so no family sibling is mid-migration during the copy (the settled-vault context snapshot-worker.mjs already relies on). verify:at-rest-migration N=4 held GREEN across 5 consecutive runs with this read-only open (2026-08-04). Reduce further by folding into snapshot-worker.mjs if their protocols ever converge.

writeCapable.why: opens :memory: for the expected-schema probe — never the real vault
writeCapable.reduceTo: verify and drop from this list

writeCapable.why: pre-migration VACUUM INTO under the init lock, against a vault other processes may be migrating
writeCapable.reduceTo: read-only IS possible in isolation (measured), but verify:at-rest-migration is too FLAKY to prove it safe on the N=4 racing-migration path — fix that gate first, then reduce

writeCapable.why: dropLegacyVaultIndex() opens THE VAULT (called with dbPath from src/db/init.js) and runs DROP TABLE IF EXISTS to remove the stale in-vault search index left by pre-sidecar builds. It was invisible to this gate until 2026-07-28: the file was wholly exempt as 'mycelium.search.db', so a fifth write-capable, latch-bypassing, DDL-executing vault opener sat behind that exemption while the ceiling claimed four.
writeCapable.reduceTo: Route the DROP through the d1 adapter so it passes assertVaultUsable(), or move the legacy-index cleanup into a migration. It runs inside initVaultStorage under the init lock, before the adapter exists, which is the only reason it opens raw today.
